name: Cherokee Syllabary
notes: Sequoyah (George Guess/Gist), a monolingual Cherokee speaker who never learned to read or write English, began work c. 1809 after observing literate soldiers during the War of 1812/Creek War; completed an 86-character (later 85) syllabary by 1821, formally adopted by the Cherokee National Council in 1825. His character shapes visibly resemble Latin/Greek/Cyrillic letterforms he had seen but could not read, while the sound values are entirely his own invention — the clean stimulus-diffusion signature. Still in active use — `latest: null`.
